table.title: [val] Co-bottleneck · Framework trade-offs
table.md:
| Option | Strengths | Weaknesses | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Server rendering | Fast first paint, good for SEO, and simple caching at the CDN edge for anonymous pages. | Every interaction needs a round trip unless you add client code, and personalised pages are hard to cache. | Default |
| Static export | Cheapest to host and trivially scalable; pages survive backend outages. | Content updates need a rebuild, which gets slow once you have tens of thousands of pages. | Docs |
| Client SPA | Rich interactions and offline support once loaded. | Slow first load on mid-range phones, and search engines may index an empty shell. | Avoid |

understanding.purpose: Compare framework options by their strengths, weaknesses, and overall verdict.
understanding.reading: Readers scan the option names, then compare the paired strengths and weaknesses before checking each verdict. Each row should remain easy to follow across the table.
groups: Strengths and Weaknesses are parallel explanatory columns and should have enough space for readable phrases.
Option and Verdict frame each comparison: one identifies the choice and the other gives its assessment.
keep_intact: Individual words and the short verdicts.
Option names where practical, especially when existing row height can accommodate a natural wrap.
may_wrap: Strengths and weaknesses can wrap at word boundaries.
Multiword option names can wrap at word boundaries.

preferred.name: r1B
preferred.note: Keep the compact Option column and shift more space to the longer Weaknesses text, testing whether its line breaks improve without making Strengths too cramped.

preferred.name: r3A
preferred.note: Keep the successful option and verdict widths from r2A, and give Weaknesses the wider measure from r2B. This tests whether a modest reduction in Strengths improves the paired explanations overall.

acceptable.name: r1C
acceptable.note: Give option names more room than r0C while retaining substantial space for both explanatory columns; test the trade-off between label continuity and prose wrapping.

acceptable.name: r2A
acceptable.note: Move 5px from Weaknesses to Strengths to test a more even pairing while trying to preserve the three-line second weakness.

acceptable.name: r2B
acceptable.note: Give Option 5px more from Strengths while retaining the Weaknesses width that worked well in r1B.

acceptable.name: r3B
acceptable.note: Keep identifiers intact and move 5px from Weaknesses to Strengths to test whether the first strengths paragraph gains a better line ending without making Weaknesses too cramped.

acceptable.name: r3C
acceptable.note: Retain r2B’s roomier Option column and r2A’s Strengths width, taking the difference from Weaknesses to test a more generous identifier column.

bad.name: r2C
bad.note: Narrow Option by 5px and give that space to Strengths, testing whether the explanatory columns can gain a better line break without disrupting the option names.
bad.why: The narrower Option column wraps “Client SPA” onto two lines, making the row labels less consistent for little visible benefit elsewhere.

rationale: The preferred layout gives the two prose columns most of the width, with a little more space for the longer weaknesses. The option labels remain easy to scan, the verdicts stay on one line, and the three data rows have a steady rhythm. The identical r1B and r3A are equally good.

general: Allocate width according to the role and content of each column, while keeping related columns visually comparable.
Preserve recognizable labels and avoid splitting words when readers need to scan across rows.
Judge wrapping and row rhythm together; a shorter table is not automatically easier to read.
specific: Strengths and Weaknesses carry most of the prose and benefit from similar widths, with a modest advantage for Weaknesses.
Verdict needs only a narrow column, while Option needs enough space to keep “Client SPA” together.

tradeoffs: A wider Option column gives labels more breathing room, as in r1C, but leaves less space for prose and adds a line to the Static export row. The other acceptable designs shift wrapping between the two prose columns without disrupting the table.
uncertain: The ranges are approximate, based on the supplied renders; widths within them should be adjusted together to stay within the 581px total. A designer could reasonably prefer r3B's more even prose columns or r1C's roomier labels.

critique.good: The paired explanatory columns have a comfortable balance, and all words and verdicts remain intact. The option labels are easy to scan, with only Server rendering wrapping.
critique.problems: The first two rows are relatively tall, and the explanatory text breaks into short phrases. The Verdict column has more space than its contents need.
critique.cause: The 190px Strengths and 206px Weaknesses widths constrain the long prose, while the 80px Verdict width takes space that could be used for comparison.

critique.good: All option names and verdicts fit on one line, making the framing columns easy to scan.
critique.problems: The prose columns are cramped, producing five-line cells and a taller table. The broad Verdict column contains conspicuous unused space.
critique.cause: The 125px Option and 111px Verdict widths leave only 165px and 180px for the much longer explanatory columns.

critique.good: This is the strongest overall balance: the prose columns carry readable phrases, all verdicts fit, and the rows are relatively compact. The first two option names wrap naturally without splitting words.
critique.problems: The narrow Option column makes Static export wrap even though its row has room to accommodate a single-line label. Weaknesses remains the limiting column in the first row, while Strengths has some spare capacity there.
critique.cause: The 85px Option width leaves 64px for text. The 216px Weaknesses width must accommodate the longest prose, while the 210px Strengths width has slightly less demanding content.

critique.good: The paired explanatory columns have a balanced appearance, all headers and words remain intact, and the verdicts are easy to scan.
critique.problems: The first two rows are tall, with the second row’s weakness ending in a short line. Both Server rendering and Static export wrap.
critique.cause: At 213px, Weaknesses forces the second weakness onto four lines. The 95px Option column does not provide enough text width for either multiword name.

critique.good: The wider Weaknesses column brings the second row down to three lines, making the table more compact while retaining readable phrases and intact verdicts. The explanatory columns still feel like a pair.
critique.problems: Both of the first two option names wrap, and the first row remains four lines tall. The Option column feels tight beside the longer explanations.
critique.cause: Option is only 85px wide. Strengths at 202px and Weaknesses at 226px still require four lines for the first row.

critique.good: Static export stays on one line, giving the option column a calmer appearance. Headers, words, and verdicts remain intact.
critique.problems: The second weakness occupies four lines, making its row taller than in r1B. The first row is also four lines tall, so the wider Option column does not reduce its height.
critique.cause: Increasing Option to 105px leaves Weaknesses at 208px, where the second weakness wraps onto an additional line.

critique.good: The option names are easy to scan: Client SPA stays on one line, while the longer names wrap naturally. The explanatory columns are balanced, and all verdicts remain intact.
critique.problems: The first strengths cell has a short final line, while the first weaknesses cell is dense. The table remains readable, but the distribution of space between those two columns could be refined.
critique.cause: The 207px Strengths column leaves “pages.” on its own line; the 221px Weaknesses column sets the longest explanation in four lines.

critique.good: The 90px Option column gives the identifiers comfortable space, and the wider Weaknesses column produces readable phrases. Verdicts remain intact.
critique.problems: The Strengths column feels noticeably tighter than Weaknesses, with shorter lines in the first row. The extra width in Option does not visibly improve the name wraps over r2A.
critique.cause: Increasing Option to 90px and Weaknesses to 226px leaves Strengths at 197px.

critique.good: The explanatory columns have a useful amount of space, and the verdicts remain compact and easy to scan.
critique.problems: Client SPA wraps even though it is a short identifier, making the option column less scannable. The first strengths cell still ends with a short line.
critique.cause: The 80px Option column leaves only 59px for text, too little for Client SPA on one line; Strengths remains at 207px.

review.method: two fresh-context blind reviews; letters shuffled; includes browser auto layout and equal widths as neutral references

r2C.why: The two explanatory columns have useful space and the verdicts scan easily. All three option names wrap, making the first column feel cramped.

r1C.why: The option column keeps two names on one line, but the narrower weaknesses column adds a line to the second row and makes the comparison columns less balanced.

r1B.why: The explanatory columns are well balanced and the verdicts are easy to scan. Two option names wrap, while Client SPA stays intact.

ref_equal.why: Wide option and verdict columns leave much unused space while the long explanations wrap into narrow, tall blocks, making comparisons harder.

r2A.why: Space is directed to the explanatory columns, with slightly more for the longer weaknesses. The rows remain compact, Client SPA stays intact, and verdicts scan easily.

ref_auto.why: The option names and verdicts have adequate room, and the table is easy to scan. The narrower strengths column produces slightly less even wrapping than E.

raw.unsure: C, E and F are close; their differences in wrapping and column balance are subtle at this size.

ref_equal.why: Equal widths leave much of the Verdict column empty while both prose columns wrap heavily, making rows tall and comparisons harder to scan.

r2C.why: The two prose columns have useful space and the verdicts remain compact. All three option names wrap, though, weakening the left-hand scan.

r1C.why: The wider Option column keeps Client SPA together and gives the labels more room, but the narrower Weaknesses column makes the second row taller.

r2A.why: Client SPA stays together, while the prose columns are balanced and wide enough to keep the rows compact. The Verdict column fits its short entries without wasting space.

ref_auto.why: The option names and verdicts scan cleanly, and the two prose columns have a balanced, compact rhythm with no awkward word breaks.

r1B.why: The columns are well proportioned: Client SPA stays together, the verdicts fit, and both prose columns wrap into readable blocks.

raw.unsure: The differences among D, E and F are very small at the displayed image size; their line breaks and overall readability appear nearly equivalent.

provenance.note: AI visual design judgement; not a human reading study
